slides.texte_overlay:
How to become extremely good
at flirting in your 20s
Start with a real question about her world. Not "Do you come here often?" Try "Okay, what's the story behind that tattoo?" Curiosity is the best opener there is, and it never sounds rehearsed.

Smile with your eyes, not just your mouth. Relax your face, slow down, enjoy the moment. A guy who looks genuinely happy to be talking to her is ten times more attractive than one trying to look cool.
Tease about small things, never about her body. "You ordered the healthiest thing on the menu, I'm judging you a little." Light and playful, then smile. If she doesn't laugh, drop it.
Share something a little personal. Not your whole life story. One real thing. "I've been trying to learn guitar and I'm honestly terrible." Openness invites openness, and that's where it gets good.
Be clear about what you want. "I had fun, can I take you for a drink this week?" Vague texts and mixed signals are exhausting. Clear and kind beats mysterious every single time.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. You'll always have a fun story ready, and being interesting is the most underrated part of flirting.

slides.texte_overlay: Take a no gracefully. "No worries, have a good night." Then actually leave her alone. How you handle a no says more about you than any line, and the people around you notice too.
